title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第17部分：推理

chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现
chapters.Objective: 3. 目标函数，精确地写出来

db0ef4310c5c.en: Here's a puzzle for a small transformer: sixteen bits. Is the number of ones odd? <bookmark mark='a'/> Trained to answer straight away, our two-layer model is right 49 percent of the time: a coin flip. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now train the very same model to write its work first: going along the bits, is the count odd so far? Each step is easy, just the last answer and one more bit. <bookmark mark='c'/> Its final answer is right 100 percent of the time. Same model, same size. It just got to think out loud.
db0ef4310c5c.zh: 给一个小Transformer出一道题：16个比特，其中1的个数是奇数吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>如果训练它直接给出答案，我们这个两层的模型，只有49%的时候答对：跟抛硬币差不多。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在，把同一个模型训练成先写出过程：沿着这些比特一路数过去：到目前为止，1的个数是奇数吗？每一步都很简单，只要上一步的答案，再加一个比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的最终答案，100%都是对的。同样的模型，同样的大小。它只不过是可以出声思考了。

750b111d3225.en: This part is about reasoning: why writing a chain of thought adds computation, how models learn to reason from nothing but a checker of answers, <bookmark mark='a'/> and what you get by letting them think longer.
750b111d3225.zh: 这一部分讲的是推理：为什么写出一条思维链，就能增加计算；模型怎样只靠一个核对答案的检查器，学会推理；<bookmark mark='a'/>以及让它们想得更久，能换来什么。

65974bccad47.en: Chapter one. Thinking out loud is computing.
65974bccad47.zh: 第1章。出声思考，就是计算。

52d606e65b07.en: Why does writing help? Look at the computation. A transformer runs every token through the same fixed stack of layers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Answering at once, the longest chain of steps that happen one after another is as tall as the stack: L layers, however hard the question. <bookmark mark='b'/> But a token it writes goes back in as input. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the chain of steps can climb the stack, come back down, and climb again, once per token. With k tokens of thought, L times k plus one steps in a row. <bookmark mark='d'/> Theory backs this up: answering at once, a transformer is limited to shallow computations; given a long enough chain of thought, it can carry out any step-by-step procedure.
52d606e65b07.zh: 写出来，为什么有用？看看其中的计算。Transformer让每个词元，都穿过同一叠固定的层。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果直接回答，一个接一个、必须先后完成的步骤，最长也只有这叠层那么高：L层，不管问题有多难。<bookmark mark='b'/>但它写下的词元，会重新作为输入送回去。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是，这条步骤链可以爬上这叠层，再回到底下，再爬上去，每个词元一次。有了k个用来思考的词元，连续的步数，就是L乘以k与1的和。<bookmark mark='d'/>理论也印证了这一点：直接回答时，Transformer只能做很浅的计算；而只要思维链足够长，它就能一步一步地执行任何程序。

d2b1ed20ba37.en: Here are all our runs, on strings of four, eight and sixteen bits. <bookmark mark='a'/> Answering at once is solved at four bits, a coin flip at eight, and a coin flip at sixteen: every bit flips the answer, and two layers can't learn to combine sixteen of them at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> With the running parity written first, that is, whether the count of ones so far is odd or even, all three are solved. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the chain is also easier to learn. At sixteen bits it's reliable after about 1,300 steps; answering at once never gets off the ground.

ac0e2bd2e923.en: Chapter two. Learning from a checker.

60f440fdcdf8.en: How do you teach a model to reason, when nobody can write down the steps for it? DeepSeek-R1 used a recipe with almost no human help: questions with checkable answers, and reinforcement learning. <bookmark mark='r'/> The model tries, gets a score, and is nudged to do more of what scored well: trial and error, not worked examples. <bookmark mark='p'/> In this game the model is called the policy, pi: the rule that gives a probability to every answer it might write. We do it here with a small transformer that has had a little practice at two-digit addition. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give it a question, and sample 8 answers. <bookmark mark='b'/> A checker marks each one: here 2 of 8 are right. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each answer's advantage is its reward minus the group's average, divided by the spread: right answers above the line, wrong ones below. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then nudge the model to make the good answers more likely and the bad ones less. <bookmark mark='e'/> That's GRPO, group relative policy optimization: each answer is judged relative to its own group. No one judges the steps. <bookmark mark='f'/> Older methods compare each reward with a baseline, the score you'd expect anyway, and train a second network, a critic, to predict it. GRPO needs no critic: the group's average is its baseline. And when every answer is right, or every one wrong, the advantages are all zero: nothing to learn.

48acda2c9144.en: Repeat that for 300 steps of thirty-two questions. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our model starts out right 36 percent of the time, and climbs to 81 percent, taught by nothing but a checker. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are its answers to six questions, eight tries each: 14 of 48 right before, <bookmark mark='c'/> 27 after. The probability moved onto the answers that check out.
48acda2c9144.zh: 把这个过程重复300步，每步32道题。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的模型一开始只有36%的时候答对，后来升到了81%，教它的，只有一个检查器。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是它对6道题的回答，每道题试8次：训练前，48个答案里对了14个，<bookmark mark='c'/>训练后对了27个。概率转移到了那些经得起核对的答案上。

bdcb54251ef7.en: What we used is an outcome reward: only the final answer is checked. <bookmark mark='a'/> The other way is a process reward: a second model, trained on people's judgments, scores every step, so a lucky guess after a wrong step earns nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Process rewards catch more, but a learned grader can be fooled, and a model under pressure learns to fool it. The big reasoning models of 2025 mostly rely on checkable outcomes: math with known answers, code with tests. Trained that way, DeepSeek-R1's chains of thought grew longer on their own, and started to double-check their own work.
bdcb54251ef7.zh: 我们用的是结果奖励：只检查最后的答案。<bookmark mark='a'/>另一种办法是过程奖励：用人的评判训练出第二个模型，让它给每一步打分；这样，错了一步之后再蒙对答案，就什么也得不到。<bookmark mark='b'/>过程奖励能抓出更多问题，但学出来的评分模型是可以被骗的，而一个被逼着拿高分的模型，就会学会去骗它。2025年的大型推理模型，大多依靠可以核对的结果：有标准答案的数学题，带测试用例的代码。这样训练出来，DeepSeek-R1的思维链自己就变长了，还开始回头检查自己的推导。

fe7796651d45.zh: 第3章。目标函数，精确地写出来。

11884414c270.en: Chapter two's recipe was the simplest version. Here is the objective GRPO actually optimizes, as DeepSeek published it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each token of each answer gets a ratio: how much likelier the model now makes it than when the answer was sampled. <bookmark mark='b'/> The advantage is chapter two's: reward against the group. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the clip. Samples are expensive, so each batch is used for several updates, and the clip keeps those updates from running away. <bookmark mark='d'/> For a good answer, the objective grows with the ratio, until the token is twenty percent likelier than it was; then it goes flat, and there's nothing more to gain. For a bad answer, it stops rewarding the push down once the token is twenty percent less likely. <bookmark mark='e'/> In our run, with four updates per batch, the clip held back 7 percent of the tokens. And the last term keeps the model near where it started.
11884414c270.zh: 第2章的做法是最简单的版本。这里是GRPO真正优化的目标函数，正如DeepSeek发表的那样。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个回答的每个词元都有一个比值：模型现在给它的概率，比采样这个回答时高了多少倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>优势还是第2章的那个：奖励和同组相比。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是截断。采样很贵，所以每个批次要拿来做好几次更新，而截断让这些更新不会失控。<bookmark mark='d'/>对一个好回答，目标函数随比值增长，直到这个词元比原来可能20%；然后它就平了，再推也没有好处。对一个坏回答，一旦这个词元的可能性降低了20%，就不再奖励继续往下推。<bookmark mark='e'/>在我们的训练里，每个批次更新4次，截断拦下了7%的词元。最后一项，让模型留在出发点附近。

217f5898e248.en: That last term needs the KL divergence, part one's measure of how far one distribution is from another, and computing it exactly would mean summing over every possible answer. <bookmark mark='a'/> Instead, GRPO uses an estimate from the sampled tokens alone, John Schulman's k three: the ratio of the starting model's probability to the current one's, minus its log, minus one. <bookmark mark='b'/> It's never negative, it's zero only when nothing has moved, and on average it equals the KL exactly. <bookmark mark='c'/> In our runs, the penalty, at weight 0.04, didn't keep GRPO closer: it ended 1.34 bits per answer from the start, against 1.24 for the plain policy gradient, chapter two's simple push on the policy, which has no penalty but takes smaller steps. At this weight the penalty is weak, and many recent recipes drop it.

abfa034960b3.en: Here is what that objective does to the model, step by step. Three questions it was unsure of, and the probability it gives each candidate answer, the right one in green. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each step, answers that beat their group's average get pushed up and the rest pushed down; the clip keeps each push small. <bookmark mark='b'/> The right answers' probability climbs from 25 percent on average to 94, and the wrong ones drain away. Not smoothly: each step learns from just eight sampled answers a question, so a right answer can drop sharply and be pulled back later. That's also why the entropy falls, from 0.93 to 0.17 bits a digit: the model stops spreading its bets.
abfa034960b3.zh: 这就是那个目标函数一步一步对模型做的事。三道它原本没把握的题，以及它给每个候选答案的概率，正确的那个是绿色。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一步，比同组平均好的回答被往上推，其余的被往下推；截断让每次推动都很小。<bookmark mark='b'/>正确答案的概率平均从25%升到94%，错误答案的概率渐渐流干。并不平稳：每一步每道题只从8个采样回答里学，所以一个正确答案可能会突然大跌，之后再被拉回来。这也是熵下降的原因，从每个数字0.93比特降到0.17比特：模型不再分散押注。

038184bb14e2.en: Before the variants, one more objective, because it explains what that KL term is really doing. <bookmark mark='i'/> The idea, in short: show the model pairs, a better and a worse answer to the same question, and raise the better one's probability, relative to the starting model, more than the worse one's. Here is where that comes from. <bookmark mark='a'/> Maximize reward while staying near the starting model. <bookmark mark='b'/> This has an exact solution: the starting model, reweighted by e to the reward over beta. <bookmark mark='c'/> Turn it around, and the reward is hidden in the best model itself: beta times the log of how much it raised each answer, plus a constant. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now suppose all we have is pairs: this answer is better than that one, with Bradley and Terry's model of preferences: the chance that one answer beats another depends only on the gap between their scores, through a sigmoid. The constant cancels. <bookmark mark='e'/> What's left is a plain loss on the model itself: push up the winner's log-ratio, push down the loser's. That's DPO, by Rafailov and colleagues: preference tuning with no reward model and no sampling during training.

579e997a8cf3.en: We tried it on our addition, with pairs of one right and one wrong answer, drawn once from the starting model. <bookmark mark='a'/> It got worse: from 35 to 24 percent right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watch the two log-probabilities on pairs it never trained on. The loss only asks the winner to rise relative to the loser, and the easiest way there was to push both down, the loser faster. The probability went somewhere, mostly to other wrong answers. This is known as likelihood displacement. Offline pairs from a weak model teach less than they seem to; the on-policy methods, which keep sampling from the model they're improving, kept getting better.
579e997a8cf3.zh: 我们在加法上试了它，用一对对一个对、一个错的回答，从起始模型里一次性抽出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>结果变差了：正确率从35%降到24%。<bookmark mark='b'/>看看在它从没训练过的那些成对样本上，两个对数概率的变化。这个损失只要求胜者相对败者上升，而最省事的办法，是把两者都往下压，败者压得更快。概率流到了别处，大多流到了其他错误答案上。这叫作似然位移。来自一个弱模型的离线配对，教会的东西比看上去少；而在线的方法，不断从正在改进的模型里采样，一直在变好。

132bc2373af4.en: Since DeepSeek-R1, a small industry has tuned this objective. <bookmark mark='a'/> Doctor GRPO drops two normalizations: dividing by the group's spread overweights questions that are nearly always right or nearly always wrong, and dividing by an answer's length lets long wrong answers off lightly. <bookmark mark='b'/> DAPO, from ByteDance, lets the clip go higher above than below, so unlikely good tokens can grow, and throws away groups that carry no signal. <bookmark mark='c'/> GSPO, used for Qwen3, takes one ratio per answer instead of per token: the geometric mean of its tokens' ratios. <bookmark mark='g'/> Multiply the ratios together and take the root, one per token, so a token that doubled and one that halved cancel out. <bookmark mark='d'/> We ran all of them, and DPO, from the same start on the same questions. <bookmark mark='e'/> The best here is DAPO, at 94 percent; the reinforcement learners span 19 points, from the same start. DPO, as we saw, ends at 24.

011c6d6739ab.en: One of DAPO's fixes is worth seeing. When all eight answers to a question are right, every advantage is zero, and so is the gradient: the question was wasted. <bookmark mark='a'/> As the model improves, that happens more and more: by the end of our run, 27 percent of the groups taught it nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> DAPO keeps sampling questions until each batch is full of groups that disagree. Here that cost 2.97 times as many questions per step.
011c6d6739ab.zh: DAPO的修正里，有一个值得看一看。当一道题的8个回答全对时，每个优势都是0，梯度也是0：这道题白做了。<bookmark mark='a'/>模型越好，这种情况就越多：到我们训练结束时，27%的组什么也没教给它。<bookmark mark='b'/>DAPO会不断抽题，直到每个批次里都装满了意见不一的组。在这里，这样做每步要多花2.97倍的题目。

8eb866e89798.en: Every one of these objectives does something else, too. <bookmark mark='a'/> It sharpens the model. The entropy of its digits falls from 0.93 bits to about 0.15: it stops considering alternatives. Too fast, and exploration dies; that's the entropy collapse that recent papers fight with <bookmark mark='h'/> DAPO's clip-higher trick from a moment ago, the lopsided clip that lets unlikely good tokens grow, and with entropy bonuses: a small reward for keeping options open. <bookmark mark='b'/> So does RL teach a model new answers, or just make it pick the ones it could already find? Yue and colleagues compared pass at k before and after RL. <bookmark mark='c'/> On ours, RL lifts one try from 33 to 87 percent, but with enough tries the two meet: both reach about 100 percent at 128. A problem this small has no answers the model can't find by chance; on hard problems, Yue and colleagues found that with enough tries the model before RL wins. RL mostly concentrates probability on answers the model already had.

0dcbb35cb955.en: There's another way to spend computation: at answer time. Take our addition model, before the reinforcement learning, and let it answer each of 200 questions 32 times. <bookmark mark='a'/> Green is right, red is wrong. Not one question is always right, and not one is always wrong: each of the 200 comes out right only some of the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> So trying again always has a chance of helping. <bookmark mark='c'/> If c of n samples are right, the chance that at least one of k tries is right is one minus n minus c choose k, over n choose k. It's called pass at k, and it needs a checker to tell which try was the right one.
0dcbb35cb955.zh: 花费计算还有另一个时机：回答的时候。拿我们那个做加法的模型，取强化学习之前的版本，让它把200道题，每道都回答32次。<bookmark mark='a'/>绿色是对，红色是错。没有一道题总是答对，也没有一道题总是答错：这200道题，每一道都只是有时候答对。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以，再试一次，总有机会帮上忙。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果n个样本里有c个是对的，那么试k次、至少有一次答对的概率，就是1减去一个比值：n减c个里取k个的组合数，除以n个里取k个的组合数。这叫作pass@k，它需要一个检查器，来分辨哪一次尝试是对的。

78471cd25224.en: So how much does trying more buy? <bookmark mark='a'/> With a checker, a lot: one try is right 33 percent of the time, and with 32 tries, 100 percent. Every doubling of the tries buys a little more. <bookmark mark='b'/> Without a checker, take a vote: the answer it gives most often. That climbs from 32 to 61 percent: less, because a vote can't recover an answer the model rarely gives. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the dashed line is the same model after reinforcement learning, with just one try: 81 percent. Training moved what used to need many tries into one. Today's reasoning models do both: trained by RL to think in long chains, and then given more time to think when the question is hard.
78471cd25224.zh: 那么，多试几次，能换来多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>有检查器的话，能换来很多：试1次，33%的时候答对；试32次，就是100%。尝试次数每翻一倍，就再多换来一点。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有检查器，就投票：取它给得最多的那个答案。这样从32%升到61%：少一些，因为模型很少给出的答案，投票是救不回来的。<bookmark mark='c'/>而那条虚线，是同一个模型经过强化学习之后，只试1次：81%。训练把原来要试很多次才能做到的事，压缩进了一次尝试里。今天的推理模型两者兼用：先用RL训练它们用长长的思维链来思考，遇到难题时，再给它们更多时间去想。

ac8eb29704db.en: Let's take stock. Writing out its steps lets a fixed-depth model compute for longer: L layers, once per token. That's how our two-layer model learned sixteen-bit parity. Reinforcement learning from a checker, comparing each answer with its group, taught a model to add more reliably than practice alone; the objective clips each update and keeps the model near where it started, and DPO turns the same idea into a loss on pairs. RL mostly sharpens what the model could already do. And at answer time, more tries buy more right answers, as long as something can tell which one is right.
ac8eb29704db.zh: 我们来盘点一下。把步骤写出来，能让一个深度固定的模型算得更久：每个词元都过一遍L层。我们的两层模型就是这样学会16比特奇偶校验的。从检查器那里做强化学习，把每个回答和同组比较，教会了模型比单纯练习更可靠地做加法；目标函数截断每次更新，并让模型留在出发点附近，而DPO把同样的想法变成了成对样本上的一个损失。强化学习主要是让模型已经能做的事变得更尖锐。而在回答的时候，多试几次就能换来更多正确答案，只要有什么东西能判断哪一个是对的。

0e4db0ff8351.en: Reasoning over many steps is what agents do, in part eighteen. Every token of thought costs time to write, which is part nineteen. And whether the chain a model writes is really how it got its answer is a question for the last part.
0e4db0ff8351.zh: 跨越许多步的推理，正是智能体要做的事，这是第18部分。每一个思考用的词元，都要花时间来写，这是第19部分。而模型写下的这条思维链，是不是它真正得出答案的方式，这个问题留给最后一部分。

6e571403cfcc.en: Next time: agents. A robot that can't see where it is keeps a belief over every place it might be, <bookmark mark='a'/> and sharpens it with each step and each glimpse of a door.
6e571403cfcc.zh: 下一次：智能体。一个看不见自己在哪里的机器人，会对它可能在的每一个位置，都保持一份信念，<bookmark mark='a'/>并且每走一步、每瞥见一扇门，就让这份信念更集中一些。

912a0e138777.en: Thanks for watching, and see you in part eighteen.

chapters_en.Outro: Recap, and where this comes back
